events.title: Heraclius defeats the Persians near Nineveh
events.description: The Byzantine emperor Heraclius routed a Sasanian army near the ruins of Nineveh in Mesopotamia. The victory ended a 26-year war, but both exhausted empires soon fell prey to the Arab conquests.
events.html: The Byzantine emperor Heraclius routed a Sasanian army near the ruins of Nineveh in Mesopotamia. The victory ended a 26-year war, but both exhausted empires soon fell prey to the Arab conquests.

events.title: Marconi receives the first transatlantic radio signal
events.description: At Signal Hill in Newfoundland, Guglielmo Marconi heard the Morse letter 'S' sent from Poldhu in Cornwall, some 3,500 kilometres away. The feat showed that radio could span oceans.

events.title: George V announces the move of India's capital to Delhi
events.description: At the Delhi Durbar, attended by hundreds of thousands, King-Emperor George V announced that the capital of British India would move from Calcutta to Delhi. New Delhi was inaugurated in 1931.
events.html: At the Delhi Durbar, attended by hundreds of thousands, King-Emperor George V announced that the capital of British India would move from Calcutta to Delhi. New Delhi was inaugurated in 1931.

events.title: Kenya gains independence with Jomo Kenyatta as prime minister
events.description: Kenya became independent from Britain. Jomo Kenyatta, jailed by the colonial authorities during the Mau Mau emergency, became prime minister and later the country's first president.
events.html: Kenya became independent from Britain. Jomo Kenyatta, jailed by the colonial authorities during the Mau Mau emergency, became prime minister and later the country's first president.

events.title: The Supreme Court halts the Florida recount in Bush v. Gore
events.description: By five votes to four, the US Supreme Court stopped the manual recount of presidential votes in Florida. The ruling left George W. Bush the winner of Florida, and of the presidency, by 537 votes.
events.html: By five votes to four, the US Supreme Court stopped the manual recount of presidential votes in Florida. The ruling left George W. Bush the winner of Florida, and of the presidency, by 537 votes.
